Data from no food but walking in the morning test on the Dawn Phenomenon

A randomized crossover study comparing the blood glucose effects of equivalent walks - same duration, same pace, same individual - in a natural environment (tree coverage dependent) versus on a treadmill in an indoor gym setting found that the nature walk produced significantly greater reductions in blood glucose (23%), cortisol, and diabetes distress scores than the treadmill walk at identical physical exertion, confirming that the natural environment adds a measurable biological benefit beyond the exercise itself. One nature walk weekly in a park or woodland with tree coverage substituted for one standard exercise session adds this cortisol suppression benefit to the standard exercise benefit.
